prompt:
Create ONE landscape 16:9 game skin illustration, not a sheet. A visibly redesigned HEIXIANG, skin theme WINTER HUNT BANQUET. Follow style images 1-4 at their broad brush scale. Image 5 is ONLY his identity, not costume or pose.

DESIGN: a massively built dark-tan adult man reclining diagonally on a carved hunting-lodge chair, one leg forward, body relaxed and head facing viewer with his recognizable amused challenging smirk. He wears a rich muted BURGUNDY VELVET long tailed formal coat fitted across his huge shoulders, an asymmetrically draped thick IVORY FUR shoulder mantle, a cream high-neck pleated cravat, a dark plum brocade waistcoat with only two large gold clasp shapes, cream tailored trousers and high oxblood riding boots. Ornate brass falcon-shaped brooch and a single pearl drop at the collar. His left forearm wears a stout dark leather falconry gauntlet, carrying a large calm white hunting falcon; his right hand loosely holds a small faceted champagne glass. A folded burgundy velvet half-mask lies beside him on the chair. NO orange scarf, combat shoulder armor, tactical pouches, black combat suit, coffee cup or giant sword. Outfit silhouette and accessories completely change.
FACE: exactly the identity in image 5: thick angular adult masculine jaw and strong nose, deep tan skin, thick eyebrows, narrow amber-gold eyes, black short hair slicked back off fully exposed forehead with gray frontal lock, shaved sides; stitched scar on HIS LEFT cheek (viewer right). Keep his original face spacing, not a generic handsome slim youth. Extremely broad shoulders, thick neck and arms.
SETTING: winter aristocratic hunt reception, lodge terrace with a simple near stone balustrade, snow-covered dark pine shapes in distance, one warm window of lodge; red drapery groups behind chair frame him. No full city, no crowded banquet tables. Quiet background with only a few broad marks, coherent perspective and ground contacts. One soft upper-left warm main light, cool snow shadows. Character centered, large readable face, full seated body intentionally within frame, coat tails and forward boot show new silhouette; his body fills 85 percent height. Eagle is secondary, not covering face.
PAINTING REFERENCE ORDER: 1 selected-baseline-v03, 2 source-5, 3 source-8, 4 wu game original; all FOUR are brushwork only. 5 heixiang is FACE/BODY IDENTITY only. Use the selected baseline's LOW DETAIL broad elongated opaque brush marks, grouped hard-edge light-shadow and quiet solid color regions. Character and setting use the same painting language. Large curved strokes shaped by form; faces and essential hands are the clearest. Sparse simplified fur clumps and velvet folds, NOT fine hair/fur/brocade patterns or stone texture. No glossy polish, no airbrush, no micro-facet triangle mosaics, no scratchy surface noise. No words, border or watermark.
STYLE: hand-painted anime illustration built from large opaque color masses and a limited set of broad directional curved or elongated strokes. Clear grouped shadows and decisive handmade edges, with a few subtle gentle skin transitions. Stroke shape communicates the turn of a form. Keep selective overlaps, broken stroke endings and expressive coverage, surrounded by quieter areas. Do not flatten every interior into uniform solid fill; do not cover every surface in brush texture.

HAIR: organize the requested hairstyle into coherent substantial locks and grouped masses, following its actual silhouette and flow. Broad curved forms, quiet base-color regions, one or a few broad shadow turns and short irregular opaque highlight swaths. Highlights sometimes break along the lock. A few deliberate tapered ends and fine contour accents are enough. Avoid hundreds of tiny facets, needle-tipped micro-locks, pale scratches, strand networks and dense flyaways.

FACE: unmistakable anime proportions, clear expressive upper-lid shapes, simple colored iris masses and a few crisp highlights. Economical nose and mouth, broad clean cheek planes. Preserve a readable fringe/temple cast shadow, small nose side/underside plane, under-jaw shadow and neck turn. A few tapered colored line accents at lower eyelids, eye folds and jaw-to-neck transitions explain anatomy. Slight warm/cool midtone turns are allowed. Keep this selective and restrained; no glossy sculpted lips or polished semi-realistic beauty shading.

BODY AND CLOTH: principal broad fold planes follow shoulder, chest, joint and torso direction under the requested clothes. Use elongated or curved opaque strokes and only a few selective crease/contour accents at collars, seams and major tension points. A couple of broad midtone turns connect the volume. Large quiet cloth areas remain. Anatomy, fingers and important props are readable without pervasive fine detail. Avoid disconnected triangular mosaics and dense wrinkle networks.

COLOR AND BACKGROUND: mostly muted colored grays within the user's chosen palette, clearly grouped light and shadow, a readable warm/cool relationship, concentrated richer color in a few focal areas. Do not impose the test character's colors. Simplify the requested backdrop with broad shapes and sparse purposeful marks, subordinate to the intended focal subject.

DETAIL HIERARCHY: faces/eyes and important gestures or props receive the clearest selective drawing; secondary clothing and surroundings are more economical. Keep the original references' confident simplified finish. Avoid photoreal skin/materials, glossy 3D, airbrushed commercial splash-art finish, all-over grain/canvas filters, tiny angular facet noise, excessive rim glow, evenly traced vector outlines and indiscriminate decorative clutter. No unrequested text, watermark or UI.
